resources.string: Android only lets apps see what\'s playing through notification access. Dot Music uses it to read the song, cover and play state of your music app. It has no internet access, so nothing ever leaves your phone.
Four sizes. Tap one to drop it on your home screen. The equaliser, the orbiting comet and the ripples are played by your launcher itself, so they cost almost no battery.
Your launcher can\'t add widgets from an app. Long-press your home screen, choose Widgets, and find Dot Music.
Draw the cover in white dots, Nothing style, instead of its own colours.
The dot equaliser, orbiting comet and ripples on the widgets while music plays.

The player ripples and the ring moves with the actual music. Android files this under the microphone permission, but the app only measures how loud each frequency is and never records anything. Off: a steady pulse instead.
No internet permission. No accounts. Your listening history stays in this app\'s private storage on your phone and is never sent anywhere.
Tap For you to play something
The player screen as a widget: the dot record with its equaliser ring, comet and ripples, title, progress and controls.

The full player, alive on your home screen: the record spins and ripples with the music, and the dots move away from your finger as you swipe between pages. Tap the record to play or pause. It only draws while you can see it, and slows down when the music is paused.
The dots appear over your own photo. Android doesn\'t let apps read your current wallpaper, so pick the same photo here once.
Show the dots on the wallpaper
Off: just your photo. Also a Quick Settings tile, so you can flip it from the notification shade.
The dots fade in when a song starts and fade away when it stops.
Your music as a spinning record of dots.
The cover as a spinning record of dots, with play and pause.
Dot record, title in dots, live equaliser and controls.
A live dot equaliser, the title in dots, play and next.
Album cover in dots. Opens the player.
Dot learns from what you play: what you finish, what you skip, what you play after what, and at what time of day. Play a few songs and your picks appear here. All of it stays on this phone.
Learned from %1$d listens, on this phone only.
Search or pick something to play
Keep listening and Dot\'s picks appear here

Dot learns from what you finish, what you skip, which songs you play after which, and the time of day. Recent listening counts more, songs you just heard get a rest, and Dot sometimes tries songs it\'s unsure about so your picks don\'t get stuck on the same ten.
Off: nothing new is recorded. What Dot already learned stays until you forget it.
Forget everything Dot has learned about your taste? This can\'t be undone.

Dot Music is a full-screen dot player with its own recommendations. Another app does the playing (YouTube Music, Dot Player, Spotify or any player you choose); Dot is the screen, the controls and the picks.
Type a song, artist or album and press search. %1$s plays the best match, and most apps keep similar songs going after it.
Next and a left flick play Dot\'s pick instead of the player app\'s queue.
Opened %1$s. It can\'t take songs from Dot directly, so search for it there.
Couldn\'t reach %1$s. Open it once, then try again.
Dot shows and controls what this app plays, learns from it, and sends its picks there. Sign in, pick audio quality and manage downloads in the app itself.
Ignore music from other apps. Off: Dot prefers the player app but also shows others.
Check what the player app supports
Shares the song title and artist
Start songs from Dot, staying in Dot
Start songs from Dot, by opening the app
\? means Dot can\'t tell yet. Play a song in %1$s, come back and check again: apps only show what they support while music is loaded.

If starting songs while staying in Dot is ✗ but opening the app is ✓, tapping a pick opens %1$s and plays it there. If both are ✗, Dot still shows, controls and learns from %1$s, and picks open it so you can search.
Sent to %1$s in the background. Did it start playing?
Sent to %1$s by opening it. Did it start playing?
%1$s doesn\'t take songs from other apps, so Dot just opened it.
